skill.name: altllm-portal-api-keys
skill.description: Manage AltLLM Portal API keys with CLI workflows for listing, creating, inspecting, updating, disabling, re-enabling, and revoking keys.
skill.summary: Guides AltLLM Portal API key lifecycle operations with the local altllm CLI.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: Most backtick execution and system reconnaissance alerts are Markdown false positives. The hardcoded URLs are confirmed low-risk external network references, and the parent-directory setup references are confirmed high-risk unreviewed instruction dependencies. Additional review found operational risks around API key confirmation, secret output handling, and production cleanup limits.

remediation.issue: Parent-directory shared instruction files are referenced from SKILL.md.
remediation.suggestion: Inline the required setup guidance or vendor the shared files inside the skill package so reviewers can audit all instructions.

remediation.issue: API key create, update, disable, and revoke flows change credential state.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation of the Portal account, target environment, action, and key ID before any state-changing command.

remediation.issue: Create responses can include full API key secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Redact full key values in chat and logs, and tell users to store the one-time secret outside the conversation.

remediation.issue: Single-key production routes are documented as broken.
remediation.suggestion: Mark get, update, and revoke as unavailable until fixed, and avoid creating temporary production keys without an approved cleanup path.

remediation.issue: Reference commands use a hardcoded production API endpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the base URL and environment with the user before running networked Portal API commands.

> Before the first `altllm` command in a fresh checkout, read and follow:
| `create-api-key` | Create a new key, optionally with a model allowlist |
| `update-api-key` | Rename a key, change status, or replace the model allowlist |
- `create-api-key` returns the full key only once.
- Flex users can allowlist normal AltLLM models and Flex-only `altllm-flex-*` models; backend access
- Do not create temporary production smoke keys unless `revoke-api-key` is healthy or an approved cl

semantic_findings.title: Credential Lifecycle Actions Lack Explicit Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The skill covers creating, updating, disabling, and permanently revoking Portal API keys. It warns that revoke is permanent, but it does not require explicit user confirmation before state-changing actions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command table and rules clearly describe state-changing credential operations. No reviewed line adds a confirmation gate before those operations.

semantic_findings.title: Full API Key Output Can Expose Secrets
semantic_findings.description: The reference output includes a full API key field, and the skill notes that the full key is returned only once. Agents could expose real secrets if they relay command output verbatim into chat or logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The reviewed files explicitly show and describe full key output. The sample value appears synthetic, but the workflow handles real one-time secrets.

semantic_findings.title: Production Backend Limitation Can Leave Keys Without Cleanup
semantic_findings.description: The skill says single-key routes for get, update, and revoke are broken in production. Creating temporary production keys while revoke is unavailable can leave credentials active without a tested cleanup path.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both files describe the broken production routes and explicitly warn against temporary production smoke keys without cleanup. The risk follows directly from the documented limitation.

content.value_statement: Portal API keys need careful lifecycle control across agents and applications. This skill guides AltLLM CLI tasks for listing, creating, updating, disabling, and revoking keys.
actual_capabilities: Lists active and disabled Portal API keys through the local altllm CLI.
Creates new API keys with optional model allowlists.
Documents inspection, renaming, status updates, and allowlist replacement for existing keys.
Documents permanent key revocation and reversible disable actions.
Explains current production limits for single-key routes.
Shows example CLI flags for the AltLLM Portal API base URL.
limitations: The skill depends on a local altllm CLI checkout and valid Portal session.
Single-key get, update, and revoke routes are documented as broken in production.
It cannot validate account tier or Flex entitlement beyond backend responses.
Created full API keys are shown only once and must be stored by the user.

use_cases.title: Set Up Agent Credentials
use_cases.description: Create a named Portal API key with a focused model allowlist for an external agent or application.

use_cases.title: Rotate Application Access
use_cases.description: List existing keys, create a replacement key, and plan disable or revoke actions for old credentials.

use_cases.title: Review Model Access
use_cases.description: Inspect documented allowlist options and status rules before changing which models a key can use.

prompt_templates.title: List Portal Keys
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the AltLLM Portal API Keys skill to list my Portal API keys for the confirmed account. Summarize active and disabled keys.

prompt_templates.title: Create Scoped Key
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Portal API key named Codex Agent for altllm-native-fast and altllm-standard. Ask for confirmation before running the command.

prompt_templates.title: Disable Existing Key
prompt_templates.prompt: Update key <key_id> to disabled after confirming the target environment. Then show the resulting status without exposing secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Production Cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the known production limitation, then propose a safe key cleanup plan before creating any temporary production keys.

output_examples.input: List Portal API keys for my active workspace.
output_examples.output: A concise summary with key names, prefixes, status values, and model allowlists.

output_examples.input: Create a key named Codex Agent with two allowed models.
output_examples.output: A confirmation request before creation, followed by a redacted result and storage warning for the one-time secret.

output_examples.input: Revoke this old key after I confirm the ID.
output_examples.output: A permanent-action warning, target key confirmation, and a status update if the backend route succeeds.

best_practices: Confirm the Portal account, target environment, and key ID before any state-changing command.
Redact full API key values from chat summaries, logs, screenshots, and tickets.
Use model allowlists to scope each key to the smallest required access.
anti_patterns: Creating temporary production keys when revoke is unavailable.
Pasting full API key values back into shared conversations or tickets.
Using the default model set when an application needs only a narrow allowlist.

faq.question: Can this skill log in to my wallet?
faq.answer: No. It is only for AltLLM Portal API key lifecycle tasks.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks the skill as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it create Flex model keys?
faq.answer: It can pass altllm-flex-* model IDs, but backend account checks remain authoritative.

faq.question: Will it show the full key later?
faq.answer: No. The source says create returns the full key only once.

faq.question: Are all key commands currently working?
faq.answer: No. The source documents single-key route issues for get, update, and revoke.

faq.question: Should I use it for billing or payments?
faq.answer: No. The skill description excludes wallet login, billing history, and payment links.
